title: Lender-Placed Flood Master Programs — Commercial Placement Schedule: Service Note and Certificate Issue Reference
content:
**Lender-Placed Flood Master Programs — Lender-Placed Flood – Commercial Building tier.**

### When the commercial placement schedule prices a certificate
For a commercial placement on the loan named on the most recently mailed first notice of a program on the Commercial Building tier, and only for such a placement, the annual premium is set by this commercial placement schedule in place of the base premium formula; a placement on the loan named on the most recently mailed first notice of a program on the Residential Mandatory Amount tier is priced by the residential placement schedule and every renewal on that tier by the residential renewal schedule, and every other certificate premium, including any on the Commercial Building and Contents tier, remains the building limit divided by 100 times the tier's building rate per 100 plus the contents limit divided by 100 times the tier's contents rate per 100, rounded to the cent, and never less than the tier's minimum certificate premium.

### Amount placed
For a placement this commercial placement schedule prices, and only for such a placement, the mandatory purchase amount is the required amount stated on the loan's latest first notice, the figure Tidemark set there as the lowest of the principal balance the lender reported, the tier's NFIP maximum building reference and the insurable value; a placement under the residential placement schedule follows that schedule's own first-notice rule, a renewal under the residential renewal schedule follows that schedule's renewal-notice rule, and for every other certificate the mandatory purchase amount remains the lowest of those three figures.

### Borrower evidence on a commercial placement
For a placement this commercial placement schedule prices, and only for such a placement, acceptable borrower evidence bars the certificate only when it was received on or after the loan's latest first notice, evidence from an earlier lapse not counting; a placement under the residential placement schedule follows that schedule's own reading, and for every other placement no certificate is issued when acceptable borrower evidence was received before placement.

### What the placement books
A new certificate on the loan, recorded as an issue entry under the program with its coverage dates and premium, and a new-placement premium charge on the program account on the statement for the current month.

### Tool reference: `issue_commercial_certificate_61c928bb`
Places lender-placed flood building and business contents coverage on one commercial loan under the lender's master program, with a newly assigned certificate number; records the borrower, the building, its flood zone, the balances and contents value the lender reports, the mandatory purchase amount, the building and contents limits, the lapse date, the coverage dates and the annual premium; bills that premium as a new placement and raises the amount the lender owes on the program by it. It is an agent-side tool, which the agent unlocks and then calls.

- `forceplaced_program_id` — reference number of the lender's master program that places the coverage, as returned by the master program lookup.
- `loan_number` — the lender's loan number exactly as shown on the borrower notices in the tracking lookup, copied verbatim.
- `borrower_name` — the borrowing business's legal name exactly as the lender states it on the call.
- `property_address` — street address of the mortgaged building exactly as the lender states it.
- `flood_zone` — flood zone on the lender's Standard Flood Hazard Determination Form; exactly one of `A`, `AE`, `AH`, `AO`, `AR`, `A99`, `V`, `VE`, `B`, `C`, `X`, `D`, `NONE` (A without base flood elevation, AE with base flood elevations, AH shallow ponding, AO shallow sheet flow, AR flood-control restoration, A99 flood-control system under construction, V coastal high hazard without base flood elevation, VE coastal high hazard with base flood elevations, B and C moderate and minimal hazard on older maps, X moderate or minimal hazard, D undetermined, NONE no zone shown).
- `outstanding_principal_balance` — unpaid principal balance as the lender reports it, USD with 2 decimals.
- `insurable_value` — building replacement cost value as the lender reports it, whole dollars.
- `required_amount` — mandatory purchase amount for the loan, whole dollars.
- `building_limit` — certificate building limit, whole dollars.
- `secured_contents_value` — value of business contents securing the loan as the lender reports it, whole dollars; 0 when contents do not secure the loan.
- `contents_limit` — certificate contents limit, whole dollars; 0 when no contents coverage is placed.
- `lapse_date` — date the borrower's own coverage lapsed or became insufficient, YYYY-MM-DD.
- `coverage_effective_date` — start date of certificate coverage, YYYY-MM-DD.
- `certificate_expiration_date` — last day of the certificate term, YYYY-MM-DD.
- `annual_premium` — annual premium, a positive USD amount with 2 decimals, rounded half to even to the cent on booking.

**Reply.** The newly assigned certificate number (letters followed by digits), the issue entry reference, the loan number, the coverage dates, the building and contents limits in whole dollars, the premium billed with its statement month (YYYY-MM), the charge entry reference and the program's amount owed net of the charge. A certificate number in the reply indicates the certificate was issued and billed.
